openwrt_wiki.Einleitung: PoE powered 802.11ax WiFi 6 access point with 8 spacial streams; approximately a 9" (220mm) disk designed for wall mounting or can be layed flat on a shelf
openwrt_wiki.Wichtig: Devices with manufacturing date 2234 (34rd week of 2022) and later appear to be a version 3 hardware with a different (1 GbE only) Ethernet PHY chip. Flashing v2 firmware to this hardware will result in inoperable Ethernet.
openwrt_wiki.v1 vs v2: v1 and v2 are not official names and thus not found in official Ubiquiti documents. Difference: v1's LED has full RGB color support while v2's has limited blue/white colors (due to supply shortages). Installing a v1 firmware on a v2 device is not fatal, just an error message around LED device initialization.
openwrt_wiki.v3: Since about summer 2022 there is a v3 device with a RTL8211 PHY. The v3 is not compatible with v1/v2 images. Use a v3 image (since 23.05). Check: dmesg | grep mtk_soc_eth (23.05.5/24.10.2: 'RTL8211F Gigabit Ethernet') bzw. dmesg | grep mtk_sgmii_init (earlier 23.05.x: 'detect RTL8211_CARD').
openwrt_wiki.Hinweis Produktion: as of early 2024, it appears that both v2 and v3 are in production
openwrt_wiki.Installation (knapp): Werksreset (Reset ~10 s), Stock-Firmware per DHCP oder 192.168.1.20 (alte Stock-Firmware 192.168.1.34), SSH ubnt/ubnt, Hardwareversion per dmesg prüfen, sysupgrade-Image per scp nach /tmp, bootselect-Flag (mtd 'bs') auf kernel0, Image per dd in kernel0 und kernel1, Neustart; erster Start ca. 4 min, danach LED dauerhaft blau. Stock-Firmware ab 6.2 hat schreibgeschützte mtd-Partitionen, das Wiki beschreibt einen Zusatzschritt (hier nicht übernommen).
openwrt_wiki.U-Boot mod: zusätzliche Variante ubnt_unifi-6-lr-v2-ubootmod: ersetzt Preloader/BL2, FIP (BL31+U-Boot), Recovery- und Firmware-Partition; nicht mit der Standardvariante mischen
openwrt_wiki.Flash Layout (Stock): mtd0 Preloader 0x40000, mtd1 ATF 0x20000, mtd2 u-boot 0x60000, mtd3 u-boot-env 0x10000, mtd4 Factory 0x40000, mtd5 EEPROM 0x10000, mtd6 bs 0x10000, mtd7 cfg 0x100000, mtd8 kernel0 0x1ee0000, mtd9 kernel1 0x1ee0000
openwrt_wiki.Debricking: TFTP-Recovery: PoE trennen, Reset halten, PoE anstecken, Reset 15-20 s halten bis LED weiß-blau-aus wechselt; Recovery-IP nicht immer 192.168.1.20 (ARP-Scan), Stock-Firmware als firmware.bin per TFTP; antwortet evtl. nicht auf Ping
openwrt_wiki.Opening the case: glued together; heat gun (~90 °C) on outer border, then sharp knife; flat knife between front and back casing below the ethernet port, then flat screwdriver; plastic clips break easily
openwrt_wiki.Serial: CPU UART0 at the pinout next to the Holtek MCU. Pinout (first pin next to SoC / MCU): 0 3V3, 1 RX, 2 TX, 3 GND. 115200, 8N1
openwrt_wiki.OEM-Bootlog: ohne Versionsangabe; MT7915 HW/SW 0x8a108a10, phy_oper_init TxStream 4 RxStream 4, Bluetooth btmtk uart
openwrt_wiki.OpenWrt-Bootlog: Linux 5.4.124 vom 2021-06-13 (v1-Zeit, Image ohne Versionsangabe): Machine model 'Ubiquiti UniFi 6 LR', Memory limited to 495MB, Memory 479932K/507580K, spi-nor w25q512jv (65536 Kbytes), mt7915e

openwrt_issue_9256.Titel: LED fails on new revisions of Ubiquiti UniFi 6 LR
openwrt_issue_9256.Text: The Unify 6 LR originally shipped with a RGB LED, newer revisions of this AP are shipped with a 'classic' Ubiquiti Blue/White LED. Datasheet: 'Due to chip supply shortages, the U6LR's LED has been limited to only white and blue color modes.' With v1 image: ubnt-ledbar 0-0030: Error initializing LED transaction; probe failed -22. Issue purely cosmetic.
